title: NATO Council Condemns Russian Airspace Violations in Poland and Romania, Underscoring Alliance Reliance on Collective (Not Just US) Response
detail: The North Atlantic Council met in Brussels on August 12, 2026 and issued a statement holding Russia "fully responsible" for a string of recent airspace violations and drone incidents over Poland and Romania, calling them "dangerous and unacceptable" and citing Moscow's "increasing tolerance for risk." Allies expressed full solidarity with Warsaw and Bucharest and pointed to steps already taken to reinforce eastern-flank air and missile defenses from the Baltic to the Black Sea. The incidents follow a July 29 cruise missile/drone crash roughly 50km from Lublin, Poland (deemed "probably Russian" by PM Donald Tusk) and repeated Romanian airspace breaches that President Nicusor Dan called "inadmissible." With the Pentagon's Europe force-posture review still underway and no new US troop commitments announced, the episode is being read in Brussels as an early test of whether the alliance's collective response mechanisms hold up as Washington pushes European allies to take primary responsibility for continental air defense.

media.caption: NATO stands with Poland and Romania amid Russian airspace violations
